policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's main text renders a first-person finite verb, "and I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days", which is the qere וָאֵשֵׁב (and I sat); the ketiv ואשר underlies only the marginal note classed textual_variant, "Another reading is, and I sat where they sat", which the translators explicitly relegate to the margin rather than adopt. The two alternative_rendering notes ("Or, sat") concern English wording and do not bear on the reading.
